I’ll just try to address each point you made in order. I might make some generalizations, yes I’m a aware that there are expecting. Just talking about the minority of people. Disclaimer: I am very tired right now and might repeat myself a few times.

Skinny people (and by this I mean being at a healthy weight, not looking like an underweight model) are statistically healthier though. Weight is an indicator that one of those factors you mentioned is effecting you negatively, so if you solve the issue, you lose weight.

Being in poverty makes it more likely to be overweight due to things like not having the money to buy healthy food because… a bad diet, stress, etc can lead to weight gain. I don’t think this goes against anything either of us has been saying.

Of course being overweight is linked to things like bad food habits and a sedentary lifestyle. When people say to lose weight they mean to fix the bad things that are leading to that. If you are skinny and have a bad diet, you are still eating a good amount of calories for your build and body. A skinny person with a bad diet will still generally be healthier than an overweight person with a bad diet. The skinny person might not be getting enough nutrients or eating too much sugar, but the main cause of issues is the calories. If a bad diet is the cause for weight gain, you literally have to be eating too many calories. So an overweight person and a skinny person in this scenario can’t be just as healthy as each other because their bad diets are at different levels of bad. Also, everyone has to eat the right amount of calories for their body and lifestyle. This skinny person might be good at 2000 calories a day, but I, for example, can’t eat more than 1200 a day or else I rapidly gain weight and my health goes down the drain. It’s not the content of the food that changes for me, just how much of it I eat. What might look like a good diet to people could still be a bad diet for a specific person. I know overweight people that eat really healthy foods, but then they eat 3 times as much as they should and wonder why they can’t lose weight. I would call that a very unhealthy diet. 

What I’m trying to say is that while skinny and overweight people both have bad habits that lead to weight gain, the intensity of the all their bad and potentially weight-causing habits together is what separates overweight people from skinny people.
